questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The destination being attractive, my expectations to being able to make local friends, the experiences in nature!

questions.answer: Yes, they were super helpful!

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very easy - many norwegians are using
Hybel.no
to find a room or apartment, so that was a very good way of finding somewhere to stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
In Bergen, you should focus on finding a place to live that suits your needs. Do you want to live a bit outside the city center to be closer to the fjells, or do you want to be able to walk to uni and around in the city. I would really recommend Sandviken, if you want to live a bit outside.
Check where busses and rent-a-bike stations are, so you're close to transportation. If transportation is easy, you never far from anywhere in Bergen. But a 6-month buscard or buy a bike – keep in mind that it is raining so bus if often very comfy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have heard very mixed experiences about living in Sammen campus. I dont know.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: the very first welcome lecture, we were given all th einformation we needed. After that I could always count on, that I would recieve an email if I needed to act on anything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The people in studentcenteret at an office, and the person at my faculty who was responsible for all exchange students

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to someone working at uni, and they will always find out if they can help you, or they can find someone who can!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had one really nice course KUVI106. I was a bit disappointed in the other course PSYK106

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The courses I took mainly had forst-year students, and I could sort of feel that, in the way the teachers were explaining some quite basic academic elements in the classes. 
The level wasn't as high as back home at UCPH, but I still really enjoyed the litterature and some of the lectures.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar, but there are a lot less amount of classes to each course compared to back home and no tasks or paper you have to work on during the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Psyk106
KUVI106

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: KUVI106 - really good teacher and at great corriculum!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Join in on a sportsteam or a club - people are super nice. 
Also be aware of posters or brochures or instagramposts about events! a lot of cool stuff are in the events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many different things! Just go to the studentcenter the event where every club is presenting themselves - you will be informed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Volunteer at music festivals! Jungelfest and Natjazz
Go to the sauna!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sognefjord, Hardanger, Finse, Tyin – just get those boots on!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, i felt like home as a dane.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to events where you know people are there to talk with eachtoher - the studentclubs for example. Or go to the sauna Laugaren - people are very open there.
Or meet people through your local roomates - say yes when you are invited!!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: When living together, you dont cook together that often, as what i am used to. People do their own thing first

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they were much more open to me than I would have expected!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bare det at du er dansker, gør det langt nemmere at møde lokale, fordi de føler sig allerede kulturelt nærmere dig end alle mulige andre. De elsker folk fra københavn hahah.
Så snart du er blevet kendt med én kan du møde deres venner.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Engage in activities where you think you can find people you would vibe with.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living the everyday life in such a cozy place, meeting so nice people, and just having the time to do whatever you want to do in this beautiful place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on my own, but it is so empowering too!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
